newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd militia says it now controls northern Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kurd militia says it now controls northern Iraq.

text.p: A Kurdish militia allied to Baghdad said on Monday it had gained control of the whole of northern Iraq after several weeks of clashes with a rival Kurdish group
"The (Kurdistan Democratic Party) KDP is in control of all the three Kurdish provinces," the KDP said in a statement.
It said an armed feud with Jalal Talabani's Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) had ended with the KDP's seizure of a key city earlier on Monday.
"The bitter and tragic episode that was caused by the fratricidal war imposed unreasonably by Talabani's PUK in their quest for total hegemony is finally over," it said.
The KDP of Massoud Barzani earlier in the day captured Sulaimaniya, Iraqi Kurdistan's biggest city and the PUK's main stronghold.
Fighting between the factions broke out last month, shattering a U.S.-brokered ceasefire.
Washington launched punitive missile attacks on southern Iraq after tens of thousands of Iraqi troops helped the KDP capture the city of Arbil on August 31.
The KDP entered Sulaimaniya, home to around one million people, unopposed, U.N. officials said.
The KDP statement said residents had forced the PUK to flee the city in an uprising as Barzani's forces homed in on the city. The PUK was not immediately available for comment.
The KDP has denied allegations from its rival that it has received further Iraqi government support since taking Arbil.
There was no sign of Iraqi government military presence when the KDP took a strategic dam on the road to Sulaimaniya earlier on Monday, witnesses said.
